releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.1
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.1 updates the bundled AnyPS5 core from v0.1.2 to **[v0.1.4](https://github.com/boykopovar/AnyPS5/releases/tag/v0.1.4)**.

## Changes
- **AnyPS5 core v0.1.4**: the bundled relinker and system libraries now come from the latest upstream release. Existing installs switch to it automatically the next time Studio starts, and each game receives the new libraries on its next launch.
- **Relink hint**: Studio now remembers which core relinked each game. If a game was relinked with an earlier core, the launch log says so and suggests relinking it in Relinker Studio if it fails to start.
- **Verified core downloads**: the bundled core is checked against the SHA-256 checksums AnyPS5 publishes for the release; a mismatch stops the build.
- The NID inspector's "Python 3 not found" message now points to the correct re-audit button.

## After updating
If a game that worked before no longer starts, open **Relinker Studio** and relink it.

**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/ramsforge/AnyPS5-Studio/compare/v1.5.0...v1.5.1

releases.name: AnyPS5 Studio v1.5.0
releases.body:
AnyPS5 Studio 1.5.0 is the biggest update so far: full controller support, playtime tracking, safer handling of your game folders, a faster app that works offline, and a round of security hardening.

## Highlights

### Full controller navigation
- Use the D-pad / left stick to move around every screen (menus, Settings, dialogs, setup and the launcher). Cross selects, Circle goes back, L1 / R1 switch tabs.
- On the game row, Left / Right still pick a game and Cross plays it; press Down to reach the game's buttons.
- Studio ignores the controller while you are playing a game, so button presses never reach Studio behind it.
- Controller rumble now follows the Haptic Feedback setting.
- Arrow keys and Escape work the same way on the keyboard.

### Playtime tracking
- Total playtime and your last session are recorded for every game and shown on the home screen.

### Safer game folders
- Studio only reorganizes folders that actually contain a PS5 title, and no longer moves game assets just because their name looks like a backup (for example `*.baked`).

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.6
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.6

- Integrated Xenia Edge upstream through November 20, 2026. This brings updates across CPU and system emulation, graphics, audio and game content handling while preserving X360 Mobile's Android features and existing fixes.
- Improved handling of game updates and Android storage access. Updated the in-game interface and input handling.
- Continued work on reducing shader-related pauses at the beginning of **Fable II**. New scenes can still pause while shaders are prepared.

Focused checks on Odin 2 covered gameplay in **GTA IV**, **Forza Horizon 2** and **Fable II**, as well as pause, resume and shutdown in **Assassin's Creed**. Results can vary across titles, devices and drivers.

TV mode, synced player profiles and picture-in-picture remain experimental. You can install this release over your current version.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 8

This update improves graphics accuracy and adds better diagnostic information for investigating driver performance reports.

## General graphics correction

- Corrected a graphics accuracy issue observed as temporary black, blue or multicoloured corruption during the opening of **Fable II**.
- The correction applies automatically and may also help other games affected by similar rendering problems. No additional game setting is required for this correction; existing recommended settings remain available.
- Verified through two opening runs reaching the first childhood gameplay scene on Odin 2. Later scenes, full campaigns and other GPUs still need testing.
- This is an accuracy improvement, with no general FPS increase promised. Brief pauses may still occur when new shaders are prepared.

## Driver diagnostics and session sharing

- Added more useful texture and performance information for investigating reported slowdowns with **RADV on Exynos/Xclipse**.
- Gameplay measurement recordings are now associated with their session and can be included when using **Share session bundle** from Session history.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 7

This update brings a general graphics correctness improvement and experimental picture-in-picture support for external media apps.

## Graphics correction

- Fixed the horizontally divided image and missing lower portion observed in the opening real-time cutscene of **Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning**.
- This is a general core correction, applied automatically without additional settings. It may benefit other games affected by similar rendering problems, but wider game and GPU coverage still needs testing.
- Verified through repeated starts and progression to character creation on Odin 2. This does not certify the full campaign or promise a general FPS increase.

## Experimental picture-in-picture

- Keep the game full screen while a compatible external media app uses Android's floating video window.
- Added an app selector with PiP compatibility indicators, an optional media link, and controls in the game menu. Find these options under **Settings → App → Appearance and startup**.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 6

Maintenance update focused on optional driver compatibility and updated game recommendations.

- Added an optional experimental texture compatibility setting for RADV on Samsung Xclipse. It is disabled by default and has not yet been verified on Xclipse hardware. Successful driver loading, rendering and performance are not guaranteed; memory use may increase.
- Added recommended settings for **Mobile Suit Gundam: Operation Troy**, restoring the visible world in the first map tested on Odin 2. A complete game copy is required; other devices and the full campaign remain unverified.
- Added recommendations for **Sonic Free Riders with the adapted No Kinect mod**. The compatible adapted mod and its designated launcher are required: settings alone do not repair the original mod, and the mod is not bundled with the app. Menus and two tutorial stages were tested; uneven steering remains under investigation, and full-game compatibility is not confirmed.

releases.name: X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5
releases.body:
# X360 Mobile 0.6.5 Hotfix 5

Maintenance update focused on game loading reliability and clearer driver diagnostics.

- Improved handling of extracted games, disc images and installed game containers.
- Added a per-game startup executable selector for games with multiple launchers.
- Improved reliability when loading additional game modules and title updates, with safer recovery after failed launches.
- Improved recognition of game files and preservation of launch preferences across library updates and shortcuts.
- More precise on-device Vulkan driver diagnostics, including the image check that failed and available error information.

Custom drivers remain device-dependent. More detailed diagnostics help investigate compatibility; they do not guarantee successful RADV loading or fix every game or mod.

Install over your current version; no uninstall is required. Keep a backup of your profiles and saves as usual.

releases.name: Cemu 2.6
releases.body:
**Changelog:**
- Exporting saves via the title manager no longer crashes when the export path contains unicode characters
- Fixed a regression in DS Virtual Console titles (#1440)
- Fixed a bug where the debug shader dumping option would try to write files to the wrong directory
- Added a right-click context menu to the PPC debugger disassembly view and fixed some smaller bugs in the debugger
- Use libusb as the backend for HID/USB devices on Windows (#1471)
- Reduce amount of Vulkan sampler objects that are created. Reduces memory usage slightly and avoids crashes on drivers that have a low limit on sampler objects
- Improved index data caching on Vulkan. This may provide a very small performance benefit in some games
- The `--force-interpreter` command line option now always uses single-threaded CPU emulation like originally intended

releases.name: Cemu 2.5
releases.body:
**Changelog:**
- Upscaling and downscaling options in the graphics settings now work correctly on Vulkan. Previously, the hermite and bicubic scaling options would only work on OpenGL and silently fall back to bilinear filtering on Vulkan
- Graphic pack support for custom scaling shaders has been reworked and is now functional on Vulkan, with fixes carrying over to OpenGL. If you are a graphic pack developer see #1392 for details
- Cemu will now show an error if the MLC directory is not writeable
- Added a workaround for graphic driver crashes seen in the eShop versions of Fatal Frame. These are caused by the game shipping with shaders that contain infinite loops. The actual hardware has an escape mechanism for this that we don't yet emulate
- Added support for connecting Wiimotes via L2CAP on Linux (Details in #1353)
- Set correct version for MacOS bundle
- Updated Arabic, German, Russian and Swedish translations

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.17
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.17: más rendimiento

### Cambios

- **Más rendimiento en procesadores con 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88/G99, MT6769/MT6789 y similares). En la versión anterior dejamos de fijar los hilos del juego a los núcleos rápidos en estos procesadores, y en algunos volvió el lag. Ahora el hilo principal del juego, el que más trabaja, va en los núcleos rápidos, y los demás hilos los reparte Android. Con 4 o más núcleos rápidos no cambia nada: todos los hilos van en ellos.
- **Menos trabajo inútil en cada fotograma.** El juego pregunta por `d3d9.dll` en cada fotograma, y el port lo anotaba en el registro cada vez: unas 2000 líneas por segundo en Most Wanted y Carbon. Ahora se anota una sola vez. Otras líneas repetitivas (texturas convertidas en la CPU, entrada de teclado, liberación de superficies) también se limitan. Además de ahorrar CPU, el registro de los reportes conserva lo importante.
- **Cierres que dejaron de aparecer.** Con la versión anterior ya no hemos vuelto a ver el cierre más repetido de Most Wanted al arrancar, ni el de Underground 2 en la preparación de los reflejos. Si te vuelve a pasar, envía el reporte desde el launcher.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.16
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.16: LAN sin bloqueos y reportes más completos

### Cambios

- **Crear carrera LAN ya no detiene el juego si tu `server.dll` es de otra versión.** Antes salía "Arranque guest detenido: server.dll: file layout does not match the lifted code" y el juego se paraba. Ahora aparece un aviso: ese teléfono no puede crear la carrera, pero sí unirse a una que cree otro jugador. Para crearla, copia el `server.dll` de la misma instalación de PC de donde sacaste el ejecutable del juego.
- **Rendimiento recuperado en procesadores con solo 2 núcleos rápidos** (Helio G85/G88, MT6769 y similares). Desde la versión anterior, todos los hilos del juego se fijaban a los núcleos rápidos. En estos procesadores eso los metía todos en solo 2 núcleos, y el juego iba peor que antes. Ahora solo se fijan cuando hay al menos 4 núcleos rápidos; si no, Android los reparte como antes.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.15
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.15: driver recomendado para tu GPU

### Driver Vulkan recomendado para tu procesador

- **El launcher te dice qué driver usar.** En *Opciones › Driver Vulkan* ahora aparece la GPU de tu teléfono y el driver que le conviene:
  - **Snapdragon (Adreno 6xx/7xx):** Turnip (Mesa), si el driver del sistema va lento o con errores gráficos.
  - **MediaTek, Exynos, Tensor o Unisoc con Mali-G57 o más nueva:** PanVK (Mesa), con la misma condición.
  - **Mali-G52/G72/G76 o más antiguas:** el driver del sistema (PanVK aún es experimental en ellas).
  - **PowerVR (Moto g54, Helio G35/G37…) y Samsung Xclipse:** el driver del sistema. No hay un driver alternativo que funcione en ellas.
- **Aviso si el driver no es para tu GPU.** Si eliges un driver hecho para otra GPU (por ejemplo, Turnip en una Mali o PanVK en una Adreno), el launcher avisa de que el juego probablemente no arrancará.

La app no incluye ningún driver: los importas tú como ZIP (adrenotools) desde el mismo diálogo.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.14
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.14: volver al juego sin cierres y reportes completos

Revisamos los reportes de la v0.1.13. La protección para GPU PowerVR funcionó: el Moto g54 ya pasa del primer dibujo. Esta versión corrige el cierre más repetido y hace que los reportes traigan la información que necesitamos.

### Correcciones

- **Cierre al volver al juego.** Si salías a otra app y volvías, el juego podía cerrarse en el primer fotograma. Android libera la ventana del juego al pasar a segundo plano, pero la superficie Vulkan seguía usándola y se destruía después. Ahora la superficie conserva su ventana hasta que se destruye.

### Reportes más útiles

- **El resumen del issue ya trae las líneas del juego.** Antes se tomaban de logcat y, cuando pulsabas *Reportar*, Android ya las había borrado: casi todos los issues llegaban con "últimas líneas del juego" vacío. Ahora salen del registro propio del juego (`game.log`), y logcat solo aporta las líneas del cierre.

releases.name: Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.13
releases.body:
## Most Wanted Android Evolved v0.1.13: mega actualización

Revisamos uno por uno los reportes y los zip de diagnóstico que nos enviaron. Esta versión corrige los fallos más repetidos y añade lo necesario para que los próximos reportes traigan toda la información.

### Gráficos

- **Detalle de las sombras ya se puede activar.** El juego solo habilita esa opción con tarjetas NVIDIA o ATI. Ahora el port se presenta como una NVIDIA GeForce 7800 GTX, así que la opción se puede subir y las sombras se dibujan en carrera.
- **Texturas DXT1 con transparencia correcta.** Se convierten a A1R5G5B5, como ya hace Carbon: menos memoria y bordes recortados correctos.
- **Protección para GPU PowerVR (MediaTek, p. ej. Moto g54 / Dimensity 7020).** El driver Vulkan de MediaTek se caía al crear el primer pipeline gráfico, en los cuatro juegos. Ahora, si el driver falla, el port reintenta con configuraciones más simples hasta encontrar una que funcione. *No hemos podido probarlo en un teléfono PowerVR; si tienes uno, cuéntanos cómo va.*

### Estabilidad

releases.name: 2.1 - November 18, 2026
releases.body: * **Start straight into a game (Wii).** Name a game when you launch DOSBox Wii and it starts with that game's config on top of `dosbox.conf`: from the Homebrew Channel (`<arguments>` in `meta.xml`) or from WiiFlow, either as a plugin (the zip now includes `wiiflow/plugins/dosbox-wii.ini`, which lists the `.conf` files in `DOSBox/Games` as games) or from its Homebrew list. A game can be named as `-gameconf <conf or folder>`, as a bare `.conf`, or as a bare folder that holds one (`autoboot.conf`, or its only `.conf`). A relative name is looked for as written, beside the launched `boot.dol`, then in the `DOSBox` folder, so a game's `.conf`, `.map` and files can all live in one folder, anywhere. If the game cannot be found DOSBox starts without one and says why on the DOS screen. The **Status** page has an **Autoboot** row, and the app now knows it was started this way (`IsAutoboot()`), ready for a single-game menu later. See the README's *Starting a game at launch*

releases.name: 2.0 - October 25, 2026
releases.body:
* **A new port.** DOSBox Wii has been rebuilt on the same [libgui](https://github.com/dborth/libgui) interface and driver framework as the other GX emulators, and no longer uses SDL. The DOSBox core is stock SVN r4301, and one codebase now builds for both the Wii and the Wii U
* **Wii U release!** DOSBox Wii now runs natively on the Wii U as its own app, with its own icon on the Wii U Menu. Requires [Aroma](https://wiiu.hacks.guide/) - run the latest Aroma release and launch the `.wuhb` directly from it
  * Full **Wii U GamePad** support - touch screen and buttons - alongside Wiimote, Nunchuk, Classic Controller and Wii U Pro Controller

### Corrigido o crash na 1ª inicialização (selecionar ROM + Start Game fechava o app)
Na primeira execução do app, depois de selecionar a ROM e tocar em **Start Game**, o app fechava sozinho; na segunda inicialização funcionava perfeitamente. Causa raiz multi-fator, todas eliminadas:

- **Ciclo do seletor de ROM quebrava a sessão gráfica**: ao abrir o seletor (DocumentsUI), a surface Vulkan era destruída/recriada e a fila de present ficava congelada — o **Start Game** na MESMA sessão rodava em estado frágil (por isso o processo limpo da 2ª execução funcionava). Each build is optimized for a specific architecture and uses a specific compiler.

releases.name: Catherine port v0.1.6
releases.body:
## The sushi bar scene, fixed for real, and shadows for the first time (v0.1.5 was a wrong diagnosis)

v0.1.5 did not fix the *Kappa Heaven* scene of the second day. The black shots were gone, but the plates and the conveyor belt that pass right in front of the camera were missing, and a dark line floated across the picture. The explanation in the v0.1.5 notes was wrong. Please update.

What was actually wrong is a bug in how the port translates this game's shaders. Its vertex shaders come in two halves, and when the port joined them it converted depth twice. That had three effects in every version that used the original depth format (v0.1.0, v0.1.1, v0.1.3 and v0.1.4):

- The near clipping plane sat at half its distance, so geometry the console cuts away was drawn. In those sushi bar shots the camera is inside a wall, and the port drew that wall over the whole shot.
- The depth buffer was squeezed into half its range (0.5 to 1), so the depth of field compared its focus settings against wrong depths. This is where the blur problems of earlier versions came from.
- The shadow maps were stored with the same wrong depth, so no cast shadow ever showed.

v0.1.2 fixed the blurred close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes but broke other shots: in over-the-shoulder shots the person speaking came out blurred while the wall behind stayed sharp. This version goes back to the original depth format and fixes the close-ups properly.

Each camera in a cutscene carries its own focus settings. For cameras placed very close (close-ups, the title screen and the piano menus), those settings only line up with the picture when they are read as if the camera's near plane were 25 units, so the port now converts them for those cameras. releases.name: v0.1.2
releases.body:
## Cutscenes and the title screen are sharp (the real fix)

Close-ups in the *Golden Playhouse* cutscenes (the ones with the black bars) could still come out blurred from edge to edge, faces included, and the title screen looked out of focus. v0.1.1 blamed a short block of shader constants; that was wrong: the depth-of-field pass never reads those bytes.

The real cause is the depth format. The game never tells the graphics API which depth range it uses, and the port assumed the OpenGL-style one, which stores depth squeezed into 0.5–1. The game's depth-of-field planes come straight from each cutscene's data and are written for a plain 0–1 depth, so a face in a close-up landed *behind* the focus plane and the whole frame got the maximum blur. When the game does not choose, the port now uses 0–1 depth, so close-ups keep the face sharp and blur only the background, as intended.

- Checked on the Flip 2: the title screen (same shot before/after: background, piano and characters go from blurred to sharp), the host's introduction, the opening credits, the opening nightmare cutscene and the first puzzle stage, at 30 fps.

releases.name: v2.0.1
releases.body:
v2.0.1 release of Skate 3 Recomp for Windows, Linux, and macOS (ARM / Experimental).

A stability and hygiene patch for v2.0.0, focused on the crash and antivirus reports from the first few hours.

## Downloads

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Stability

- Fixed a crash on Linux and macOS where the game could die suddenly during gameplay when world streaming revoked memory the renderer was reading
- Fixed distant demoted tree trunks rendering with a flat blue texture

#### Antivirus false positives

- The Windows executable and runtime DLL now carry proper version metadata, and the runtime no longer contains any ability to create executable memory (it never used it - all game code is compiled at build time); both changes target the machine-learning heuristics some antivirus engines were tripping on
- A false-positive report has been filed with Microsoft for the v2.0.0 files; if your antivirus quarantined the runtime, restore it or re-download this release

#### Diagnostics

- The game now logs its exact build version at startup, so support logs identify the build they came from

Use the new v2.0.2 release for critical fixes.

v2.0.0 release of Skate 3 Recomp for Windows, Linux, and macOS (ARM / Experimental).

Skate 3 now renders natively. This release replaces the emulated Xbox 360 GPU with a new renderer built directly on Direct3D 12 and Vulkan: more than double the frame rate at around a quarter of the GPU power draw, and on macOS a jump from roughly 25 FPS to 250 FPS at 4K. The entire game renders natively at close visual parity with the console output, with a set of optional modern graphics enhancements that seek to go beyond it.

The new native renderer is early and is likely to have issues, I haven't tested the game all the way through.

## Downloads

- Windows: `Skate3Recomp-Windows.zip`
- Linux: `Skate3Recomp-Linux.zip`
- macOS: `Skate3Recomp-macOS.zip`

## Changes

#### Native renderer

- New native renderer on Direct3D 12 and Vulkan, enabled by default, replacing the emulated Xbox 360 GPU
- More than 2x the frame rate at about a quarter of the GPU power draw; macOS goes from ~25 FPS to ~250 FPS (at 4K render scaling, excluding the optional enhancements like PCSS shadows)

releases.name: v0.7.7
releases.body:
v0.7.7 fixes the Android surface orientation: the v0.7.6 build restored the identity-preferred swapchain preTransform that had shipped in v0.7.5, and on devices reporting ROTATE_90 the composer applied that rotation a second time to an already-upright window-space blit. The game UI rendered sideways and the touch overlay and cursor left the visible area, which is why the on-screen cursor and some options panels (e.g. the Display tab) did not appear where expected.

This release returns the swapchain preTransform to the current display transform, so the composer no longer adds an implicit rotation. Framebuffer, touch overlay, and cursor share one orientation again.

- `preTransform` is now `cap.currentTransform` in `nvn_vulkan.c` (the code path that shipped in the working v0.7.4 build), instead of identity-preferred. Log line `[vulkan-surface-transform]` prints the supported / current / selected masks each session; expect `selected` to equal `current`.

releases.name: Termux-Aether 1000.0.0
releases.body:
## Pacman suite (packaging revision 2)

Download **`termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz`** and its `.sha256` file. This is a real Pacman package:

```sh
sha256sum -c termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz.sha256
pacman -U ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

It directly owns the native runtime and API commands and stages both APKs under `$PREFIX/share/termux-aether-suite`. Update Android apps using `aether-apks api`, then `aether-apks app`; Android confirms these updates. Existing app IDs, signatures and data paths are preserved. Shizuku and Arch images remain optional.

If you previously installed Aether commands manually, download `aether-install.py` and its checksum too:

```sh
sha256sum -c aether-install.py.sha256
python aether-install.py --adopt-legacy ./termux-aether-suite-aarch64.pkg.tar.xz
```

This backs up only the nine known unowned legacy commands and transfers ownership to Pacman. Unrelated files/packages are refused. No wildcard overwrite or editing of checksum-protected scripts is needed. Use `aether-update` for later protected upgrades, or install new suite packages with `pacman -U` directly.

releases.body:
# FusionHUD v1.1

Brings FusionHUD up to date with the HUD in [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) (main `b74261e6`). The HUD files are byte-identical copies of Bannerlator's, with only the license header added.

## New in the HUD
- **Pill size:** battery temperature as a `BAT °C` chip next to RAM, and a GPU name that is wider than the stats gets its own line across the top.
- **MediaTek GPUs:** GPU load and clock are read from MediaTek's GED nodes.
- **Charging state:** when Android reports no charge state, it is read from `/sys/class/power_supply` instead.
- **Config fix:** a config string with a single setting (for example just `hudSize=pill`) is no longer ignored.
- **Optional readouts your app can set** (nothing is drawn until you set them):
  - `setPresentedFps` — frames reaching the screen next to the game's own rate when something adds or drops frames after the game, e.g. `60→120` with frame generation or `60→45` when frames are lost.
  - `setDisplayServer` — `X11` or `Wayland`.
  - `setHdrState` — an HDR status line (`FusionHdr` codes).
  - `setGpuSpoofName` — the GPU name reported to games, marked "(spoof)" on the GPU row.

## Demo app

releases.name: FusionHUD v1.0
releases.body:
# FusionHUD v1.0

**FusionHUD** is a lightweight, forkable in-game performance overlay for Android (Winlator / Wine / PC-emulation projects) — the MangoHud-inspired HUD extracted from [Bannerlator](https://github.com/The412Banner/Bannerlator) so any project can adopt it.

## What you get
- **The Fusion HUD** — one overlay, **5 tap-cyclable sizes** (Full / Tiles / Pill / Minimal / Mega) with toggleable per-metric chips.
- **A hardened, cross-vendor metric backend** — FPS + frametime graph, CPU (aggregate + per-core), GPU %/clock/temp, thermals, RAM/VRAM, battery (with the **mA/µA current-unit auto-detect** that fixes `0.0W` on OEMs like HONOR), and network — with graceful fallbacks across **Adreno · Mali · PowerVR · Xclipse**.
- **Diagnostics export** for triaging metric gaps on unusual devices.
- Composited ~1 Hz off the present path — designed not to cost frames.

## How to adopt it
- **Gradle (JitPack):** add JitPack and depend on `com.github.The412Banner:FusionHUD:v1.0` — or grab the **`fusionhud-release.aar`** attached below.

# YukiHub v0.4.5 更新日志

> 本次更新聚焦：**四平台游玩状态同步 · Hikarinagi 快捷登录优化 · SD 卡目录授权 · 稳定性修复**

## ✨ 全新功能

- **同步游玩状态至四个平台**：现在可以把本地的游玩时长与进度，一键同步到 **NextMoe·未萌（鲲 Galgame）**、**VNDB**、**Bangumi** 与 **Hikarinagi**。四个平台的入口统一收进个人资料页的「同步游玩状态」折叠卡，点开后按平台逐项操作，状态一目了然。
- **Hikarinagi 快捷登录支持邮箱识别**：现在用 Hikarinagi 快捷登录时会一并读取邮箱，若该邮箱已在 YukiHub 注册过，**将直接登录并绑定到原账号**，与 NextMoe·未萌 的行为完全一致，不再另开新号、云同步数据也不会分裂。

## 🎨 体验优化

- **内置 Gal 工具箱常规维护**：同步更新内置工具箱里的网址与内容，保持可用。
- **同步进度弹窗重做**：进度展示改为环形进度 + 分步状态，四个平台的同步过程都能清楚看到当前在做什么。
- **新增取消绑定游玩状态同步凭证**:打开对应窗口后，长按即可弹出取消，清空凭证以重新登陆。
- **bangumi游戏自定义查询新增id查询**:因api缺陷，部分游戏不能直接搜到，因此新增了id搜索，在自定义搜索界面，直接输入数字is即可。

## 🛠 问题修复

- **修复 NextMoe 源封面模糊的问题**：部分作品封面会取到低分辨率图，现已修正取图逻辑。
- **修复通知权限疯狂弹窗的问题**：此前会反复请求通知权限，现已正常。
- **修复 SD 卡授权时选不到指定文件夹的问题**：内置文件选择器新增 SD 卡支持，现在可以正常选中 SD 卡里的游戏目录。

## 📌 说明

- **同步范围**：VNDB 不支持通过 API 写入游玩时长，因此同步到 VNDB 时只同步状态。
- **首次同步需要授权**：各平台同步需先在对应平台完成一次授权，之后会在后台自动使用。
- **Hikarinagi 登录**：已用旧方式登录过的老账号不受影响，仍会登录原来的账号；新登录会自动识别邮箱。
- **升级不影响存档**：本次更新不涉及引擎与存档逻辑，原有存档数据可正常读取。

---

感谢每一位玩家的反馈与支持，祝游玩愉快！🎮

## What this release fixes · 本版修复

**EN**

- Porting some games stopped at the "GLSLC capture" stage with a build error
  and produced nothing (Eastward and Tokyo Xanadu eX+ were reported). The
  capture works again: games that compile their shaders at run time port
  through now.
- Pressing "Update runtime" on a game's page rebuilt the runtime without the
  game's per-build tables, and Unreal-engine games crashed at startup
  afterwards (FINAL FANTASY RESONANCE, Octopath Traveler 0, DRAGON QUEST VII
  Reimagined). The rebuild carries the game's full build data now.
- The build page's progress reads correctly, and installing a game no longer
  retranslates every shader (@mijuu, #79).

**Before you update**: your games keep the runtime they have and play exactly
as before — the fixes take effect when you port again or press "Update
runtime". If a game of yours crashes at startup after a rebuild, press it once
more after updating: the game starts, and your saves were never at risk.

**中文**

- 一些游戏的移植停在"GLSLC capture"阶段并报构建错误、没有产物(已收到
  Eastward 与 Tokyo Xanadu eX+ 的报告)。现在可以正常通过:运行时自己编译
  着色器的游戏能移植了。
- 在游戏页面点"Update runtime"重建运行库时会丢掉游戏的 per-build 数据表,

### The assistant is in the app

The app carries an assistant now. It runs on the phone itself, in the same
Linux environment the porting tools run in, so no computer is involved. Ask
it in your own words - why a game crashed, why a port would not build, what
is in the library - and it reads the game's log, the build's output and the
library's state by itself. It answers in the language you write to it.

A game that misbehaves goes to a case worker: it opens a case file for that
game - the symptom, the cause, the fix it proposes - and its steps are
visible while it works. A code change waits until you say yes. The knowledge
it diagnoses with ships inside the app: over 400 upstream porting cases,
sorted by what you see, searchable and offline.

To talk to a model the assistant needs one of your own: the Settings tab
takes a provider, a model and a key, and the key stays on the phone.
Without a key, everything else in the app works exactly as before.

### Porting on the phone

A merged dump - one file holding the base game, its update and the DLC
together - now ports as its own version; it could pick the wrong patch or

### The gamepad and the touch stick

The face buttons of a controller are one choice now: by position (the Switch's
layout - X on top, Y on the left, A on the right, B at the bottom) or by what
the controller prints. It is set per controller in the gamepad center and takes
effect at once. The per-key rebinding is gone: it needed a capture flow and a
binding table, players got lost in it, and a rebound button took another key's
source away without anyone seeing why. The center's scope shows what the game
receives, so pressing a button is the test.

The controller's axes are read the way that controller reports them. The Xbox
family (a USB xpad, a Bluetooth XInput pad) puts its triggers on Z/RZ and its
right stick on RX/RY - the opposite of the usual layout - so those pads'
triggers never fired and their right stick never reached the game. The app now
works the roles out of the device's own ranges.

The touch stick starts where the thumb lands: the offset is taken from the
point the finger went down, so a thumb on the rim has output right away. A
small dead zone around that point, the rim is the full deflection, and the
right stick is finer at low speed.

## Before you update · 更新之前(必读)

- (EN) This build fixes the runtime build on the phone. If you have not imported the profiles package of v0.4.0-alpha01 yet, you still must: the app runs the games on the new host (0.4.0), and the old package's packs were built for the previous one. Import it in the environment check (the "manage" box).
- (中文) 本版修复了手机上的运行库构建。如果你还没有导入 v0.4.0-alpha01 的档案包，现在仍然必须导入：App 用新宿主(0.4.0)运行游戏，旧档案包的数据包是按旧宿主构建的。到环境检查里(那个"管理"按钮)导入。

## Fixed: the runtime a game needs on the phone builds again

The new host (0.4.0) checks every profile's picture - the screenshot the README shows - and looked for it in the app's own tool folder, where the pictures are not shipped: the build failed with "readme_image 'docs/images/...': no such file in the repository", and every game whose profile names a picture could not be rebuilt. The check now runs where the pictures are (a checkout of the repository), and the app's own copy leaves it out. Sixty games had a picture in their profile: all of them build now.

The fix is in the app, so the runtime on the phone is rebuilt as soon as the app is updated. Nothing to import for this one.

---

### 修复:游戏在手机上需要的运行库又能构建了

## Before you update · 更新之前(必读)

- (EN) This release moves the packs onto a new host (0.4.0). After the app updates, you **must** import the new profiles package in the environment check (the "manage" box): the old package's packs were built for the previous host and will not work with this app. The app will remind you and point you there. Update the app first, then import the package - both steps are required.

## New games: NieR:Automata, Link's Awakening, Silver Pines

Three games join the profiles package:

- **NieR:Automata The End of YoRHa Edition** - boots with update 1.0.3, and the map is drawn correctly after loading a save. Broader gameplay checks are still pending, so expect rough edges.
- **The Legend of Zelda: Link's Awakening** - playable on update 1.1.0, verified on a Lenovo TB323FU. It runs at a dynamic 30/60 fps by default; the stable-60 option stays off (it can judder on weaker chips). It needs the firmware files.
- **Silver Pines** - the v65536 update (1.0.1) plays, verified on the Xiaomi 23117RK66C (Android 16).

releases.name: 0.20.5 - Balance, Bugfixes
releases.body:
# MHGU Recomp 0.20.5

- Added optional "Rebalanced" preset to the monster HP scaling settings
    - This makes monster health scaling closer to what it is in newer-gen titles, like MH Rise (easier for 1 player, harder for 3-4 players)
    - This is *not* the default setting and probably never will be. You have to click the "Rebalanced" preset to use it. You can switch back by clicking "Original" at any time
    - In multiplayer hubs, the hub host's setting is always used. You do not need to change your settings to match the host, it will temporarily change automatically until you leave the hub
    - The reason for this preset is that the game is a slog in solo hub, but gets quite easy with 3-4 players and hunts are over very fast. I recommend you try it out! You might like it.
- Fixed a bug in GU where Bowgun critical distance changes at higher framerates, resulting in damage loss for bowguns
- Fixed a bug in GU where certain monster melee attacks "miss" the player more often at higher framerates (because of hitboxes not staying active long enough) 

Thanks a lot to the issue reporters and people who helped me with research for the high framerate bugs! (#23)

releases.name: 0.20.4 - Deviant Quests Shared, Bugfixes
releases.body:
# MHGU Recomp 0.20.4

- Added setting to share credit for clearing Deviant Quests! That means everyone gets credit for clearing the quest, not just the poster. This should make Deviant Quests a lot more enjoyable when playing with groups
    - This setting is enabled by default
    - This only clears quests that you "should" have access to. If your friend is 1 quest ahead and you complete that Deviant quest together, it will not count retroactively (as with village quests in the hub)
- Added support for Switch 2 Pro Controllers
- (Android) Added rumble for devices that have controller rumble but report that they don't (like the AYN Thor)
    - If you are playing this on your phone, this likely means that your phone will vibrate! You can turn off rumble in the *ingame* main menu options if it's annoying
- Weapon icons for unknown weapon types (like modded weapons) now show up as a large red "X" in the Search Hubs list and in the hub player list, instead of a Greatsword icon

releases.name: 0.20.3 - Bugfixes, mods
releases.body:
# MHGU Recomp 0.20.3

- Made most mods load and perform *much* faster, particularly large content-adding mods
- Changed `subsdk` mod handling to be much more accurate to emulators
- Fixed a lot of Steam Deck and Steam Controller annoyances that caused the `SELECT`+`START` settings menu and the "Are you sure you want to exit?" prompt to misbehave
- Fixed MHXX-style 2nd screen on dual-screen devices (like the AYN Thor) not accepting touch input properly
- Half-fixed a bug in GU where at high framerates, Pierce Shots from Bowguns and most Bow shots did not deal the correct amount of damage
    - This should fix the infamous "Lao HBG speedrun at 60 FPS not getting the head break" bug at 60 FPS
    - Thanks a lot to the reporters for their detailed reports! (#23)
    - This bug is not 100% fixed, and rears its head again at 120+ FPS, but at a smaller scale. I'm looking into it!
- Fixed a bug where the game would crash before saving if a lot of mods were installed
- Fixed a bug where you could very rarely get a "The hub server runs a different version" message
- Added improved logging for mod conflicts
- Fixed timezoneservice log spam in log.txt files

# MHGU Recomp 0.20.2

- Made most mods load and perform *much* faster, particularly large content-adding mods
- Fixed a lot of Steam Deck and Steam Controller annoyances that caused the `SELECT`+`START` settings menu and the "Are you sure you want to exit?" prompt to misbehave
- Changed `subsdk` mod handling to be much more accurate to emulators (this might temporarily break something, please open an issue if you are a mod author and find your mod is broken by this update!)
- Fixed MHXX-style 2nd screen on dual-screen devices (like the AYN Thor) not accepting touch input properly
- Half-fixed a bug in GU where at high framerates, Pierce Shots from Bowguns and most Bow shots did not deal the correct amount of damage
    - This should fix the infamous "Lao HBG speedrun at 60 FPS not getting the head break" bug at 60 FPS
    - Thanks a lot to the reporters for their detailed reports! (#23)
    - This bug is not 100% fixed, and rears its head again above 120 FPS, but at a smaller scale. I'm looking into it!
- Fixed a bug where the game would crash before saving if a lot of mods were installed

# MHGU Recomp 0.20.5

- Added optional "Rebalanced" preset to the monster HP scaling settings
    - This makes monster health scaling closer to what it is in newer-gen titles, like MH Rise (easier for 1 player, harder for 3-4 players)
    - This is *not* the default setting and probably never will be. You have to click the "Rebalanced" preset to use it. You can switch back by clicking "Original" at any time
    - In multiplayer hubs, the hub host's setting is always used. You do not need to change your settings to match the host, it will temporarily change automatically until you leave the hub
    - The reason for this preset is that the game is a slog in solo hub, but gets quite easy with 3-4 players and hunts are over very fast. I recommend you try it out! You might like it.
- Fixed a bug in GU where Bowgun critical distance changes at higher framerates, resulting in damage loss for bowguns
- Fixed a bug in GU where certain monster melee attacks "miss" the player more often at higher framerates (because of hitboxes not staying active long enough) 

Thanks a lot to the issue reporters and people who helped me with research for the high framerate bugs! (#23)

releases.name: dsr-native-loader v0.5.0
releases.body:
## What's new?

- **Native touch camera control:** You can now move the game camera by simply swiping your thumb! There is also a camera sensitivity setting found inside the Touch tab to adjust the speed. This is now the default camera control, but the old camera stick can still be selected under "Camera control" in the Touch tab.
- **Texture disk cache:** Converted textures are now saved to storage and reused the next time you play, instead of being converted again. This means shorter freezes when loading into areas you've been before on GPUs that can't read BC textures (such as Mali). Found under GPU settings. Thanks to @Juniorpamonha 
- **BC texture support for Mali:** Mali GPUs using the malisx2 driver can now read the game's textures directly without converting them, along with improved BC7/BC6H texture decoding. Thanks to @fernanfez00 
- **Bundled-in malisx2 driver:** There is now an available malisx2 driver to select for Mali GPUs. v0.6.1
- **Quit button:** A quit button has been added next to the close button in the settings menu.

releases.name: dsr-native-loader v0.4.0
releases.body: ## What's new? - **Touch control skins:** Support for custom touch control skins as well as a new default skin brought to you by @v39192503-ux !! - **Simpler logging:** Logs by default are now much smaller and create less frequently to reduce file sizes and save storage. Detailed logging can be re-enabled inside the settings tab. - **FSR Upscaling:** You can now upscale the game from any resolution using FSR! Even the standard 720p! Brought to you by @fernanfez00 - **Sharp UI:** When enabled and using a lower render resolution, the HUD, the UI, and text all render at the device's native resolution. - **Shadow quality:** Options to reduce shadow quality or turn it off altogether. Turning it off improves performance on low-end devices. - **Culling:** Hides what you cannot see to improve performance. Found under experimental GPU settings as "Skip hidden objects". Here thanks to @fernanfez00

releases.name: dsr-native-loader v0.3.0
releases.body:
## What's new?

- **Cheat support:** You can now import or write your own cheat text files similarly to how you would on Eden emu.
- **Unlocked FPS option:** When this is selected the fps now caps itself to your screens refresh rate. (Expect bugs and glitches playing above 60FPS)
- **Included optional Turnip driver for Adreno:** I have tested the turnip driver on an Adreno 740 and 630 and both seem to run better using the newly included v39 driver compared to system default. If any graphical issues occur use the system driver, or a different custom driver.
- **Lighter post-processing option**
- **More Mali gpu optimizations**
- **Slight performance optimizations overall**
## Fixes

- A crash that may occur during Ornstein & Smough or Centipede Demon fight at 60fps

releases.name: v0.1.3 — Adreno 8xx picture fix, PC-style weapon/camera controls, cloth setting
releases.body:
**Still an early test build.** Install it over the previous version: saves and settings stay.

### Fixes
- **Adreno 8xx (825, 830, 840, ...): picture fixed.** Bundled the Turnip T30 driver by Mr_Purple_666 (https://github.com/MrPurple666/purple-turnip, Mesa, MIT), which players confirmed runs these GPUs fine. No need to copy a driver by hand anymore.
- **Controls follow the game's PC layout:** the weapon button opens the four weapon groups (rifles / fists & grenades / pistols / SMGs; before it only picked SMGs); the grenade button was bound to a wrong key and is gone (grenades are in "fists").

### New
- **Camera button** (centre the camera behind Vito) in "more"; in the car: **camera** (switch view), **radio** (next station), **look back** (hold).
- **Cloth physics setting** (Auto / High / Medium / Low) in the gear menu: lower = less CPU load.
- **Faster CPU code**: indirect calls cached per call site (about half of the call-lookup cost gone).
- The gear menu's "Voice" entry is gone (it needed a separate fan pack).

### Reporting bugs: logs are required

releases.name: v0.1.2 — Adreno 8xx graphics, lighter cloth physics, menu arrows
releases.body:
**Still a very early test build.** Install it over the previous version: saves and settings stay.

### Fixes
- **Adreno 8xx (810, 825, 830, 840, ...)**: Turnip now draws in a safer mode (system memory) on all of them, for the graphics glitches reported on the Adreno 830.
- **Less CPU load**: the cloth simulation (coats, jackets) took about a third of the CPU. It is now much cheaper: fewer solver iterations on low and medium "Game graphics" (low 2, medium 3, high keeps the game's 5) and faster code. Less heat on long sessions.

### New
- **Menu arrows**: on-screen up/down/left/right buttons in the menus, so you don't have to steer the cursor.

### Reporting bugs: logs are required
Please attach **both** `mafia2-native.log` and `app_process64_d3d9.log` from `Android/data/com.mafia2re.game/files/`, plus your phone model. Reports without logs can't be fixed. The issue form asks for them.

### Known issues
- Phones with old CPU cores only (Cortex-A53/A73, e.g. Snapdragon 625/660/665) are not supported.
- Mali GPUs with Vulkan 1.1 drivers can't run it; low-end GPUs (e.g. Mali-G57) are too slow.

releases.name: v0.1.1 — Adreno 8xx and Mali fixes, cutscene sound, English, gyro aim
releases.body:
**Still a very early test build.** Install it over v0.1.0: saves and settings stay.

### Fixes
- **Crash on start with Adreno 8xx (830, 840, ...)**: the bundled Turnip driver was wrongly rejected, so the game fell back to Qualcomm's driver and crashed. Turnip is now detected properly.
- **Adreno 810 and 825**: added to the bundled Turnip (they were "unsupported" and crashed). Untested on real devices yet; please report.
- **Oversaturated, too dark / too bright picture on some Mali GPUs** (e.g. Mali-G615): fixed.
- **No sound in pre-rendered cutscenes and intro logos**: movie audio now plays.

### New
- **Game language**: English by default when the English files (`pc/sds_en`) are present, switchable in the settings ("Game language").
- **Voice**: English speech with Russian text (fan pack as `pc/sds_ru_en`).
- **Gyro aim**: settings → "Gyro aim": off / while aiming / always.
- **Aim as a toggle**: one tap to aim, the next to stop (settings → "Aim").

### Known issues
- Phones with old CPU cores (Cortex-A53/A73 only, e.g. Snapdragon 625/660/665) are not supported.
- Mali GPUs with Vulkan 1.1 drivers (e.g. Mali-G68 on some phones) can't run it.

releases.name: v0.1.0 — first test build (very early)
releases.body:
**First test build. The project is at a very early stage:** expect crashes, graphics glitches, slowdowns and lost progress.

### Requirements
- Android 10+, arm64. Tested on a Pixel 6 (Mali-G78) only.
- Your own copy of **GOG Mafia II (the 2010 original, not the Definitive Edition)**. The APK has no game files.
- On phones weaker than a Pixel 6 the game may run badly or not start at all.

### Installing
1. Copy the game's `pc` and `edit` folders to `Internal storage/Android/data/com.mafia2re.game/files/game` (or to `Internal storage/Mafia II`).
2. Next to them, a `physx` folder with `PhysXCore_283.dll` and `NxCooking_283.dll` from the PhysX installer in the game's `Redist` folder.
3. Install the APK and start it.

Language: the game runs in the language of your files. With a Russian copy you can add:
- English text and speech: the `pc/sds_en` folder of an English install next to `pc/sds_ru`, then "Game language: English" in the settings;
- English speech with Russian text: the fan pack's `sds_ru` folder as `pc/sds_ru_en`, then "Voice: English".
The DLC episodes keep the language of their own files.

### What works

releases.name: 0.10.0-alpha: in English and Spanish
releases.body:
**SMRPG Recomp for Android**: an unofficial port of *Super Mario RPG* (Nintendo Switch, 2023, version 1.0.0) to Android by static recompilation, on top of the [LASRecomp](https://github.com/peiikai/LASRecomp) runtime. It is an **alpha**.

### What's new

- **The settings menu is in English**, and in Spanish when the game's language is Spanish (Video > Game language). With "Automatic" it follows the system's language.
- The whole repository is in English now: code, log messages, scripts and documents. The README is also [in Spanish](https://github.com/ElKiro1311/smrpg-recompiled-android/blob/main/README.es.md).
- New names, in English, for the HD texture folders (`textures/` and `textures-dump/`) and for the test environment file (`env.txt`). The earlier ones still work.

**Updating from 0.9.1-alpha:** install the APK on top. Your saves, your settings and the game code you already built (`lasgame.so`) stay as they are: there is nothing to build again.

> **Legal notice.** A non-profit fan project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Nintendo or Square Enix. *Super Mario RPG* and *Mario* are trademarks of Nintendo; the game is © Nintendo / SQUARE ENIX. Neither the APK nor the repository contains any of the game's files, code, graphics, music or text. You need the files of **your own copy** of the game, already extracted (the `exefs` and `romfs` folders of version 1.0.0); there are no instructions here on how to obtain them.

### Installing

1. Install `smrpg-recomp-android-0.9.1-alpha.apk` (Android 13 or newer, 64-bit ARM, Vulkan 1.3).
2. Compile the game's code for your device (`lasgame.so`) from your extracted copy, on a Windows PC: [README, "Building"](https://github.com/ElKiro1311/smrpg-recompiled-android#building). The APK contains nothing of the game, so it can't do this step for you yet.
